subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should maintainers require a current-main Windows/WSL second-build repro before choosing a tsdown-wrapper/dependency fix, or approve a broader rollback away from tsdown now?
rationale: The report is credible and affects a supported build path, but the proposed rollback is a broad build-system direction that automation cannot choose safely without live repro and maintainer ownership.

options.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
options.body: Ask for or run first-build and second-build logs on current main, then decide between dependency update, pin, wrapper cleanup, or rollback from isolated evidence.

options.title: Sponsor immediate build-tool rollback investigation
options.body: Treat the screenshot as enough beta-blocking evidence and have maintainers evaluate a tsc rollback with full build/package proof before merge.

options.title: Link to the cleanup PR only
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94109 as related context, but do not make it canonical unless it proves the same second-build hang on Windows/WSL.

recommendation.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
recommendation.body: Ask for or run first-build and second-build logs on current main, then decide between dependency update, pin, wrapper cleanup, or rollback from isolated evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter asked @steipete for the build-tool decision, and current history shows Peter Steinberger as the strongest recent owner of the wrapper/config surface.
